investigations.name: actin-to-membrane-force-handshake
investigations.title: Coupler A · Actin→membrane force handshake
investigations.objective: In the closed-loop flexible composite, is the force the actin side reports at the interface equal-and-opposite to the force the membrane integrates on its receiving vertices (Newton's 3rd law on the coupling interface)?
investigations.claim: OBSERVED (option B, magnitude-conserving): the coupler now sizes the osmotic offset so its integrated membrane force equals the actin contact force; force_residual ≈ 0 every step. CAVEAT: pressure-mediated effective-force handshake, not an independent per-vertex check (that is option A, blocked by a pymem3dg applied-force segfault — tracked).

investigations.name: coupled-ratchet-cycle-fv-reproduction
investigations.title: Benchmark · Coupled force–velocity reproduction
investigations.objective: Does the closed-loop coupled cycle reproduce the Inoue-2015 concave→convex F-V transition as polymerization rate varies — the headline numerical benchmark for a flexible-membrane ratchet (spec §1.2)?
investigations.claim: TARGET (not yet tested): the closed loop reproduces the Inoue-2015 concave→convex F-V transition. No benchmark comparison has been run.

investigations.name: fixed-boundary
investigations.title: Rung 1 · Fixed boundary
investigations.objective: Does the composite reproduce the rigid-wall Peskin-1993 regime — Brownian-ratchet kinetics against an immovable boundary — to within numerical tolerance, when barrier_kind is "fixed"?
investigations.claim: OBSERVED (partial pass): against an immovable wall mean barrier_velocity = 0 (within ±1e-3) while contact force accumulates. Quantitative match to the Peskin ratchet rate still pending a digitized reference.

investigations.name: flexible-mem3dg-boundary
investigations.title: Rung 3 · Flexible Mem3DG boundary
investigations.objective: With barrier_kind="flexible" (closed-icosphere Mem3DG mesh inside-pushed by bonded actin filaments), does the membrane deform under actin pressure and relax the contact-force burden compared to the rigid_movable rung?
investigations.claim: OBSERVED: under actin pressure the vesicle inflates. That load is redistributed across filaments / relaxed off the rigid curve is NOT yet quantified — inflation alone is not ratchet success.

investigations.name: membrane-to-actin-displacement-feedback
investigations.title: Coupler B · Membrane→actin displacement feedback
investigations.objective: Does per-step mesh-position feedback from Mem3DG to ReaDDy preserve mesh quality (no vertex inversion or degenerate triangles) and keep tip particles within their box-potential bounds?
investigations.claim: TARGET (not yet tested): per-step mesh-position feedback preserves mesh quality and keeps tips inside their box potentials. Mesh-quality is currently inferred, not measured.

investigations.name: rigid-movable-boundary
investigations.title: Rung 2 · Rigid movable boundary
investigations.objective: With barrier_kind="rigid_movable", does the wall translate at a velocity proportional to the mean contact force (drag-balance Peskin 1993 setup), and does the stall force remain bounded?
investigations.claim: OBSERVED: a drag-loaded movable wall settles to a non-zero velocity. Whether the stall force stays within the Peskin-1993 bound is NOT yet checked.
